cd /workspace && git clone https://git.savannah.gnu.org/git/cflow.git /workspace/cflow 2>&1 | tail -5 & git clone https://github.com/robertdavidgraham/masscan.git /workspace/masscan 2>&1 | tail -5 & wait && echo "Both repositories cloned"
ls /workspace/cflow/ && head -50 /workspace/cflow/README 2>/dev/null || echo "No README" && cat /workspace/cflow/configure.ac 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo "No configure.ac"
cd /workspace/cflow && cat bootstrap.conf | head -20 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; ls -la bootstrap 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; head -30 bootstrap 2>/dev/null
apt-cache search cflow 2>&1 | head -10
apt-get install -y cflow 2>&1 | tail -5 && cflow --version 2>&1 | head -3

ls /workspace/cflow/gnulib/ 2>/dev/null | head -10; echo "---"; ls /workspace/cflow/gnulib/lib/ 2>/dev/null | head -10; echo "---"; cat /workspace/cflow/.gitmodules 2>/dev/null || echo "No .gitmodules"
cd /workspace/cflow && git submodule update --init 2>&1 | tail -20
ls /workspace/masscan/ && echo "---" && ls /workspace/masscan/src/ | head -30
ls /workspace/masscan/src/*.c | wc -l && echo "---" && ls /workspace/masscan/src/*.c && echo "===" && head -50 /workspace/masscan/Makefile
cd /workspace/masscan && grep -E 'INCLUDES|FLAGS|CFLAGS|DEFINES|CC ' Makefile | head -20
cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow --cpp='gcc -E -dD' -I. --main main 2>&1 | head -50
cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' main.c 2>&1 | head -50
cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' -w *.c 2>/dev/null | head -100

cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' *.c > /tmp/cflow_test.txt 2>&1; echo "Exit code: $?"; wc -l /tmp/cflow_test.txt; grep -v "redefined\|previous definition" /tmp/cflow_test.txt | head -50

mkdir -p /analysis-results && cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' *.c 2>/dev/null > /analysis-results/cflow-call-graph.txt && echo "Main call graph saved. Lines: $(wc -l < /analysis-results/cflow-call-graph.txt)"

cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -r -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' *.c 2>/dev/null > /analysis-results/cflow-reverse-call-graph.txt && echo "Reverse call graph saved. Lines: $(wc -l < /analysis-results/cflow-reverse-call-graph.txt)"

cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -f posix -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' *.c 2>/dev/null > /analysis-results/cflow-posix-format.txt && echo "POSIX format saved. Lines: $(wc -l < /analysis-results/cflow-posix-format.txt)"
cd /workspace/masscan/src && cflow -b -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' *.c 2>/dev/null > /analysis-results/cflow-brief.txt && echo "Brief format saved. Lines: $(wc -l < /analysis-results/cflow-brief.txt)"

cd /workspace/masscan/src && mkdir -p /analysis-results/per-module && for f in main.c main-conf.c stack-tcp-core.c proto-tcp-app.c proto-banner1.c massip-rangesv4.c templ-pkt.c rawsock.c output.c; do cflow -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' "$f" 2>/dev/null > "/analysis-results/per-module/cflow-${f%.c}.txt" && echo "Generated cflow-${f%.c}.txt: $(wc -l < /analysis-results/per-module/cflow-${f%.c}.txt) lines"; done

cat > /analysis-results/analysis-summary.txt << 'SUMMARY'
================================================================================
cFlow Analysis of masscan - Summary Report
================================================================================

Tool: GNU cflow 1.7 (installed via apt on Ubuntu 24.04)
Target Project: masscan (https://github.com/robertdavidgraham/masscan)

GNU cflow is a control flow analyzer for C source files. It generates a
call graph showing which functions call which other functions, producing
a hierarchical tree structure of the program's control flow.

- Include path: -I. (current directory)

Output Files:

4. cflow-brief.txt            - Brief format (without parameter declarations)

Key Findings:
- The analysis shows the complete call hierarchy starting from main()
- The main() function in main.c is the entry point

  * Network scanning: stack-tcp-core.c, proto-tcp-app.c
  * Banner processing: proto-banner1.c, proto-banout.c
  * Raw socket operations: rawsock.c and related files
  * IP range management: massip-rangesv4.c, massip-rangesv6.c
  * Packet templating: templ-pkt.c, templ-payloads.c

cd /workspace/masscan/src && head -30 proto-tcp-app.c && echo "---" && cflow -v 2 -I. --cpp='gcc -E -dD' proto-tcp-app.c 2>&1 | head -20

echo "=== Main call graph (first 30 lines) ===" && head -30 /analysis-results/cflow-call-graph.txt && echo "" && echo "=== POSIX format (first 20 lines) ===" && head -20 /analysis-results/cflow-posix-format.txt

echo "=== Analysis Results Directory ===" && find /analysis-results -type f -exec ls -la {} \; | awk '{print $5, $9}' && echo "" && echo "=== Total files: $(find /analysis-results -type f | wc -l) ===" && echo "=== Total size: $(du -sh /analysis-results | cut -f1) ===" && echo "=== Source files analyzed: $(ls /workspace/masscan/src/*.c | wc -l) C files ===" && echo "=== cflow version: $(cflow --version | head -1) ==="

* Introduction

This file contains brief information about configuring, and installing
GNU cflow. It is *not* intended as a replacement for the

* History

The GNU cflow was initially written in 1997, when I needed a utility
that could display the control flow in a C program. The latest updates
in its old repo date back to 1999. Then, as I no longer needed the
package, it fell into oblivion.

Six years later a thread in gnu-devel mailing list had shown that
there is a kind of demand for that sort of utility, so I decided to
resurrect it and make a full-fledged package of it. On 2005-04-12 it
was dubbed a GNU package.

* Current Status

The package is fully operational. It compiles and runs on any
GNU/Linux and most decent UNIX-like systems. It supports all command
line switches required by POSIX, plus a number of extended ones. It is
able to produce output in two formats: in GNU cflow format (which is
the default) and in POSIX format.

Currently the utility is only able to process C sources. It is the
only deviation from POSIX specs, which requires ability to process
YACC and LEX sources as well as binary object files. This support will
appear in future versions.

Emacs module cflow-mode.el works with files in GNU cflow format (as
opposed to POSIX format). It has been tested with Emacs 24.2.1.

on how to use configure. There is currently only one package-specific
configuration option: --enable-debug, which compiles the package with
